change: Share only overlapping exact bundle GETs within a compatible publication batch; bounded owners/waiters, caller deadlines, no completed cache, independent member extraction and replay. Archive/admission/memory limits unchanged.

control.label: control
control.method: Frozen control 0b07410 versus batch-scoped sharing of overlapping bundle GETs, control first at 20 writers. Completed reads are evicted before notification; independent member binding/replay and original read deadlines remain. Two counters record read owners and joined callers, not successful GETs. No mutation retry is added. Same per-reply eight-frame transport window, archive batch size two, four archive-cut slots, 256-MiB admission budget and 4096-entry cap. Three pinned 1-vCPU/3-GiB nodes, 1500 three-voter groups, 500 leaders/1000 followers each; four SQL workers/64 reservations; 20 writers, two 180-second windows. Fresh persistent internal node data and unchanged external RustFS backing, cold VM each cohort. No timed retries. Exact 4500 replicas/1500 archives, all errors retained. Boundary host/compiler/VM CPU observations. No builds, profiling or preservation by this task during timing. All artifacts retained; historical cohorts relocated with verified content/metadata and original volume paths before both runs. Closed historical Raft logs were losslessly compressed and verified before this pair.

method_limits: Control first at 20 writers after profile restoration. Prior 24-writer pair used candidate-first order; differing loads prevent treating it as identical-load reversed confirmation.
Successful latencies exclude refused requests; any timed error fails qualification.
Operation durations overlap and are not additive client latency components.

Reconcile successful SQL stages to successful writes. Failed or abandoned admission waits remain separate from successful outcomes. Bundle read owner/join counters are logical admissions including later failure/cancellation, not successful GET or avoided-byte counts.

When failed timing omits normal final resource/peak-memory snapshots, these fields remain unavailable, not zero; independently verified initial limits, timed CPU boundaries and postfailure data checks retain their own scope.
Boundary VM/cgroup counters differ in timing and cannot be exactly subtracted.
Coverage index distance includes protocol entries; boundary lag is not admission retained-entry count.

decision.reason: Neither the 24-writer nor the control-first 20-writer pair demonstrates a qualified sustained gain. The latter has lower successful TPS and higher p99 in both candidate windows; both complete repeat sets fail the zero-error gate. Shared-host observations do not prove causal regression. Restore the previously measured control instead of retaining unqualified read-sharing complexity.
